content: {"rule":"K-S2","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge makes the divided treatment of Isaiah 7:14's virgin/young-woman wording and prophetic application the reason for UNDERDETERMINED, which is the kind of two-sense treatment K-S2 governs.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"D5 vs C5 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- Challenger answered the virgin and young-woman wording in [DR3] and defender answered the prophetic application in [CR2] and [CR3].","rule_words":"That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.","room":"A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand. Reading 1: this bars treating the virgin/young-woman and prophetic-application answers as a two-sense split that leaves the verse UNDERDETERMINED. Reading 2: K-S2 only bars a single-verse-does-not-state ground, not noting that each side answered a different aspect.","why":"The rule says a verse with two senses at once is not open and both senses stand, so the judge's UNDERDETERMINED on that split breaches K-S2."}
